title: The Related Key Boomerang Attack on ChaCha Permutation Function †
abstract: The ChaCha stream cipher is widely employed in both hardware and software implementations. Although its security has been extensively studied through differential and differential-linear cryptanalysis, its vulnerability to variants of differential cryptanalysis remains largely unaddressed. This paper investigates the related-key boomerang attack on the ChaCha permutation function. The boomerang attack leverages differential analysis by decomposing the primitive into two sub-components, an approach that proves particularly efficient in cases where identifying high-probability differentials over the entire primitive is infeasible. The related-key boomerang attack incorporates four distinct yet related keys alongside the input differentials to mount the attack. This paper presents a related-key boomerang analysis of the ChaCha 6 and ChaCha 7 permutation functions. Additionally, an attack algorithm targeting reduced-round variants of ChaCha is presented, establishing a correlation among input differences, output differences, and key-bit positions. Consequently, we propose a distinguisher for the ChaCha 6 permutation function with a data complexity of approximately 22.03. Furthermore, we evaluate the ChaCha 7 variant and demonstrate that, for certain attack configurations, it exhibits no detectable bias, thereby establishing a well-defined security boundary for this attack.

title: 基于自适应的图论的图神经网络
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) based on adaptive graph theory, leveraging the inherent structure and feature representation of graphs to automatically optimize network parameters. Traditional GNNs often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their ability to effectively capture complex graph dynamics. Our proposed algorithm dynamically adjusts the network's parameters based on the graph's topology, enabling enhanced model generalization. The core mechanism involves constructing a dynamic graph representation and employing a learned parameter adjustment strategy. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of experiments on benchmark datasets, showcasing improved performance compared to existing methods.

title: 基于动态的贝叶斯网络结构优化
abstract: This paper presents a novel method for optimizing model parameters within a dynamic Bayesian network (DBN) framework. Traditional approaches often rely on static structure definition, which can limit the model's flexibility and hinder generalization. Our proposed method utilizes a dynamically evolving BDD to learn optimal model parameters and automatically adjust model structure, resulting in enhanced model performance. We introduce a "Dynamic Bayesian Network Structure Optimization" mechanism that adapts the BDD's structure during training, facilitating better generalization. The paper details the methodology, presents experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness, and discusses the benefits and limitations of this approach.

title: Non-Linear Geometry Topology and Information Encoding with Quantum Entanglement
abstract: This paper explores the potential of non-linear geometry topology to revolutionize information encoding and quantum entanglement. We propose a novel protocol leveraging dynamic topology, a fundamental concept in geometry, to achieve unparalleled security for quantum information. The core mechanism involves introducing a 'dynamic topology' framework, allowing for the encoding of complex information through quantum entanglement, offering enhanced resilience against decoherence and noise. We demonstrate the protocol's effectiveness through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation, highlighting the potential for creating robust and secure quantum communication systems.

title: Quantum-Guided Wave Function Optimization for Molecular Design
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum-guided wave function optimization to molecular design, aiming to accelerate the discovery of novel molecules with tailored properties. We introduce a novel quantum algorithm that employs quantum interference to guide the optimization process, leading to enhanced structural analysis and ultimately, the identification of optimal molecular configurations. The core mechanism centers around the creation of a quantum circuit to explore the molecular space, leveraging quantum mechanics to overcome limitations inherent in classical optimization techniques. The research explores the potential of this approach to surpass traditional methods in generating designs with superior performance characteristics. The paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and preliminary results, highlighting its unique capabilities and potential impact on the field of molecular design.

title: 基于生物启发神经网络的混沌系统预测
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to chaos system prediction utilizing a biologically-inspired neural network. Traditional methods for chaos prediction often struggle with the inherent complexity and sensitivity to initial conditions that characterize chaotic systems. This research proposes a neural network architecture designed to mimic the adaptive and dynamic properties of biological neural networks, specifically incorporating synaptic plasticity and evolving connection patterns. The core mechanism involves training the network on the dynamics of the chaotic system, allowing it to learn the underlying equations and subsequently forecast future states. The resulting model demonstrates the potential to overcome the limitations of conventional chaos prediction techniques by leveraging the self-organizing capabilities of these networks. The key innovation lies in the application of a biologically-plausible network structure to address the challenges of chaotic system prediction, offering a potentially more robust and accurate forecasting strategy. This work aims to provide a foundational approach for future research in applying bio-inspired neural networks to complex dynamical systems.

Traditional optimization methods often struggle with complex environments, necessitating pre-defined parameters. This framework leverages the unique properties of high-order matrices to dynamically adjust parameters, enabling a more flexible and efficient optimization process for quantum computation. We present a theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the efficacy of this approach in optimizing quantum circuit parameters, ultimately leading to improved performance. The core mechanism focuses on intelligently tuning the matrix's structure to address specific challenges within quantum algorithms.

title: Quantum State Adaptive Topology Transformation via Gaussian Processes
abstract: Quantum state adaptive topology transformation aims to provide a novel framework for manipulating and modeling quantum states. This paper proposes a method based on Gaussian processes that dynamically adjusts transformation rules, offering precise control over complex system behavior. We introduce a framework where the transformation process is intrinsically linked to the system's dynamics, enabling a more efficient and flexible approach to quantum state manipulation. The core mechanism leverages Gaussian processes to define the state's adaptive evolution, providing a robust and controllable method for quantum system modeling. The proposed approach demonstrates a significant improvement in accuracy and efficiency compared to existing techniques, particularly in complex systems exhibiting non-linear dynamics.

title: 基于动态概率模型的自适应强化学习
abstract: This paper introduces a novel reinforcement learning framework, termed "Dynamic Probability-Based Adaptive Learning" (DPAL), designed to enhance learning efficiency and performance through dynamic adjustment of learning strategies. Traditional reinforcement learning algorithms often struggle with environments exhibiting dynamic changes, necessitating static models that fail to adapt effectively. DPAL employs a dynamic probability model to continuously update the agent's policy based on feedback and model improvement, ensuring a responsive and adaptable learning process. We explore the framework's efficacy through theoretical analysis and preliminary experiments on a simulated environment, demonstrating significant improvements in learning speed and final performance compared to existing methods. This work offers a promising approach to address the limitations of traditional reinforcement learning by incorporating dynamic adaptability.

title: Based on Simulated Evolution Algorithm for Hardware Circuit Design Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to hardware circuit design optimization leveraging the Simulated Evolution Algorithm (SEA). The core idea is to utilize SEA's inherent search capabilities to automatically explore and optimize the topology and parameters of hardware circuits, ultimately meeting specified performance requirements. Traditional circuit design often relies heavily on manual optimization or predefined design rules, which can be time-consuming and may not always yield the most efficient solutions. SEA offers an automated and potentially more effective alternative. This work details the implementation and application of SEA to a simplified digital circuit, demonstrating its ability to produce designs with improved performance metrics. The algorithm iteratively evolves a population of circuit designs, with better designs – those achieving higher performance – being selected and mutated to generate new designs. The key contribution lies in the application of evolutionary principles to a domain where optimization is highly complex and often dominated by constraints. This research highlights the potential of SEA as a tool for accelerating and improving the design of complex hardware circuits.

title: Quantum Entanglement's Non-Classical Geometry Model
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, offers a unique paradigm for computation and information processing. This paper explores the potential of leveraging this phenomenon through the development of novel geometric models, specifically designed to harness the inherent properties of entangled quantum systems. We propose a new approach that utilizes non-classical geometry to fundamentally reshape probability logic and arithmetic operations, aiming to overcome the limitations of current quantum computing paradigms. The core mechanism centers around constructing geometric structures that encode and manipulate quantum information in a fundamentally different way, expanding the possibilities for quantum algorithm design and enabling new computational paradigms. This research addresses the inherent challenges of leveraging entanglement for practical applications, potentially leading to breakthroughs in quantum information theory and algorithm development.

title: Artificial Intelligence in equivocal prostatic needle biopsies: benign mimics and cancer detection
abstract: BACKGROUND: Equivocal prostatic needle biopsies are diagnostically challenging because minute atypical glandular foci may represent early acinar adenocarcinoma or benign mimics. This review critically examines the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in small-focus cancer detection, recognition of benign mimics, and immunohistochemistry (IHC) triage. METHODS: A structured narrative search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, and Google Scholar was conducted from database inception through 15 May 2026. English-language, peer-reviewed diagnostic and validation studies, consensus recommendations, and focused reviews addressing prostate needle-biopsy interpretation, benign mimics, IHC, digital pathology, and clinically relevant AI methods were included. RESULTS: AI applied to digitized H&E slides can support cancer detection, grading, workflow prioritization, and quality assurance. In equivocal biopsies, its most credible near-term roles are localization of minute suspicious foci and safety-prioritized identification of cases in which IHC might be avoided or requested earlier. However, partial atrophy, adenosis, basal cell hyperplasia, seminal vesicle or ejaculatory duct epithelium, inflammation, treatment effects, and tissue or scanning artefacts may cause clinically important errors. Current evidence is mainly retrospective, and equivocal cases are often defined by previous IHC-ordering practice rather than uniform morphological criteria. Clinical use requires mimic-enriched external validation, conservative thresholds, interpretable localization, and pathologist-led correlation with morphology and IHC.

title: Frequency-Modulated Spiral Manifold: A Model for Temporal Knowledge Graph Completion
abstract: Temporal knowledge graph completion (TKGC) infers missing facts by modeling the temporal evolution of relations. Existing methods typically encode time through low-dimensional geometric transformations or frequency-domain decomposition. However, periodically recurring relations can still be mapped to overlapping trajectories in the same two-dimensional working space, which may reduce temporal separability and produce conflicting optimization signals. To address this limitation, we propose the Frequency-Modulated Spiral Manifold (FMSM) model, which includes the following: (1) a relation-adaptive spectral partition and relation-dimension gate for fusing long- and short-term relation channels; (2) an independent global phase embedding and nonlinear spiral push that lift entangled planar trajectories onto separated three-dimensional manifold layers; and (3) a spiral norm regularizer that stabilizes temporal evolution while preserving valid burst signals. The artificial-intelligence contribution of FMSM is a phase-conditioned spectral-geometric representation that separates recurring temporal facts while retaining multi-scale relation dynamics. Its engineering application is the completion of time-stamped event records for dynamic knowledge-based decision-support systems. Experiments on ICEWS14, ICEWS05-15, and GDELT show that, compared with the strongest reported baseline TeRDy, FMSM yields relative MRR improvements of 0.62%, 0.86%, and 13.28%.

title: Local gradient neural operator
abstract: Field temporal prediction and source identification constitute canonical problems in dynamical systems. Conventional approaches to these problems depend on a thorough understanding of the governing partial differential equations (PDEs). Recently, deep learning, as represented by neural operators, has provided a data-driven paradigm for addressing such tasks. However, most existing global neural operators for PDEs require large training datasets and many learnable parameters, with limited interpretability and generalization. We propose the local gradient neural operator (LGNO) as a lightweight and interpretable alternative for field temporal evolution prediction and source identification in typical mechanical problems. The method builds on priors from nonlinear gradient discretization and uses multilayer perceptron convolutional layers to learn translation-invariant local kernels that resemble discrete stencils. A zero consistent stencil factorization separates coefficient learning from field reconstruction, rendering the learned operators more transparent. For problems with symmetries, network folding shares equivalent components and reduces parameter counts. We evaluate the method on PDE benchmarks covering linear and nonlinear, static and dynamic, and low and high dimensional cases. Results show that LGNO maintains accuracy, parameter efficiency, and rollout stability across these tasks, and further exhibits wide applicability to mechanical problems including diffusion, flow, and quantum phenomena.

title: Stable-MM-R1: Anchoring Multimodal Reasoning Dynamics via Entropy-Guided Stratification
abstract: While Reinforcement Learning (RL) effectively incentivizes reasoning in Large Language Models, current pipelines are hindered by training instability and rapid entropy collapse. These limitations often stem from "Rollout Silencing" and low-quality gradient signals in standard sampling procedures. In this work, we propose a robust, data-centric framework to stabilize RL training. We first introduce Potential-Aware Query Mining (PAQM), which filters data dynamically to focus on the "Distillation Zone"---samples with high potential for capability elicitation. Furthermore, we present Hybrid Stratified Replay (HSR), a novel mechanism that restructures batches by stratifying rollouts based on Path Entropy, a rollout-level confidence proxy, and outcome reward. Within each optimization step, HSR reuses current-policy "Stability Anchors" and "Hard Negatives" to construct high-contrast optimization groups, then clears its buffers before the next step. This approach mitigates entropy collapse while improving the utilization of learning signals under limited compute. Our method outperforms strong baselines on complex reasoning tasks, offering a principled solution for stable and efficient RL fine-tuning.

title: LLM Agents as Computational Typologists
abstract: Linguistic typology relies on expert analysis of reference grammars across languages, making large-scale crosslinguistic comparison labor-intensive and unscalable. We introduce AUTOTYPOLOGIST, an LLM agent for evidence-grounded typological analysis over reference grammars. The agent is capable of retrieving relevant grammar sections, analyzing interlinear glossed text (IGT), and iteratively reasoning over typological hypotheses using a ReAct-style workflow. We evaluate the system on TYPOLOGICAL FEATURE CODING against expert annotations and TYPOLOGICAL HYPOTHESIS TESTING with typological universals using 25 open-source reference grammars. Operating under different information constraints in TYPOLOGICAL FEATURE CODING, the agent can synthesize information from reference grammar prose but still faces challenges with only IGTs in the target language. In TYPOLOGICAL HYPOTHESIS TESTING, the agent can synthesize crosslinguistic evidence and identify both supporting cases and counterexamples. These findings suggest that LLM agents can support scalable and inspectable typological analysis, while still requiring expert validation.

title: ML AND DL CROSS-DOMAIN ANALYSIS ASSESSING THEIR INFLUENCE IN VARIOUS DOMAINS
abstract: Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) technologies are indispensable in the fields of solving complex problems across different application areas. In this study, the authors compare cross domain use of ML and DL algorithms across three industry sectors—healthcare, natural language processing (NLP), and network security. The pre-processing of publicly available benchmark datasets was performed on the data using Data Cleaning, Normalization, Feature Selection and Text Preprocessing methods. A total of 4 ML algorithms (Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM and CatBoost) and 4 DL algorithms (CNN, LSTM, GRU and Transformer) were tested on classification accuracy. The outputs show that the deep learning models generally outperform the machine learning algorithms with the highest accuracy in all the domains being achieved by Transformer and XGBoost being the best-performing machine learning algorithm. This research points out advantages and disadvantages of both strategies, and guides selection of appropriate algorithms in a variety of real-world applications.

title: Dynamic Geometry Transformations and Gaussian Processes
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for dynamic geometry transformations and Gaussian processes, designed to automatically adjust geometric transformation parameters based on input data dynamics. Traditional geometric transformations often rely on static parameters, limiting their adaptability and creative potential. Our approach leverages a dynamic adjustment mechanism driven by data, offering a more responsive and intuitive solution for geometric representation and modeling. We explore the core concept of dynamically adjusting transformation parameters to achieve more natural and flexible geometric expressions.

title: Algorithmic Decentralized Consensus for Distributed Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper investigates the challenges of achieving consensus in distributed quantum computing, a critical requirement for building a robust and scalable quantum network. Traditional consensus algorithms often struggle with the inherent complexity and potential for manipulation of quantum states. We propose a novel algorithmic decentralized consensus mechanism that leverages quantum superposition and entanglement to create a distributed ledger, offering enhanced data integrity and resilience against attacks. The core mechanism involves a 'quantum-assisted verification' process, which utilizes quantum properties to detect and correct inconsistencies in the quantum state, thereby establishing a verifiable and tamper-proof consensus. The paper details the design of the algorithm, its security proofs, and potential applications, emphasizing the advantages of this approach over existing solutions.

title: Dynamic Parameter Adjustment
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to quantum parameter adjustment – Dynamic Parameter Adjustment (DPA). The core concept revolves around leveraging quantum entanglement and superposition to dynamically adjust quantum system parameters, offering a potential pathway to optimize quantum system performance across a broad range of applications. Traditional parameter adjustment methods, often reliant on manual intervention, struggle to effectively handle complex, multi-dimensional problems. This research proposes a method that dynamically adapts to these challenges through the application of quantum entanglement and superposition, providing a fundamentally new paradigm for parameter control. We present a detailed theoretical framework and preliminary experimental validation demonstrating the efficacy of this approach.

title: Quantum Computation Tensor Mapping & Parallel Computing
abstract: Quantum computation, leveraging the principles of quantum mechanics, offers unprecedented computational capabilities compared to classical computation. This paper explores the application of tensor mapping within quantum computing to enhance parallel processing capabilities. We propose a novel framework, Quantum Tensor Mapping & Parallel Computing (QTMPC), which utilizes the unique properties of tensor mappings to efficiently map large datasets to quantum computers, achieving significant improvements in computational efficiency and scalability. The core mechanism centers around the strategic application of tensor mappings to exploit quantum entanglement and superposition for parallel computation. The paper details the framework's architecture, discusses its advantages over existing parallel computing techniques, and provides a preliminary analysis of its performance.

Specifically, we introduce an optimization algorithm designed to enhance the efficiency of entanglement calculations. This research offers a significant advancement in the field by providing a dynamically adaptable and computationally efficient method for understanding and controlling the complexity of quantum entanglement.

title: Quantum-Inspired Relational Reasoning for Data Clustering
abstract: Data clustering remains a fundamental problem in machine learning, driven by the need to extract meaningful patterns and structures from complex datasets. Traditional relational reasoning approaches, based on distance metrics and graph algorithms, often struggle to effectively capture intricate relationships, particularly within high-dimensional spaces. This paper proposes a novel approach – Quantum-Inspired Relational Reasoning (QIRR) – that draws inspiration from quantum mechanics, specifically superposition and entanglement, to address these limitations. QIRR represents data points as probabilistic entities, exploring potential relationships concurrently through a mechanism analogous to relational entanglement. The core idea is to quantify the "relational entanglement" between data points, leading to probabilistic cluster assignments. Unlike conventional relational methods, QIRR doesn't rely solely on distance calculations but incorporates a probabilistic framework that can better handle ambiguity and complex correlations. We present the theoretical framework, detailing the mathematical formulation of QIRR, including the concept of relational entanglement probability (REP) and its role in cluster formation. The approach offers a potentially more robust and scalable solution for data clustering, especially for datasets exhibiting intricate and high-dimensional relationships. We demonstrate the core principles with a conceptual framework and outline potential future research directions.

title: Relational Neural Networks with Dynamic Embedding Projection
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to relational neural networks (RNNs) that addresses the limitations of static embedding techniques. We propose a dynamic embedding projection layer within an RNN architecture, allowing node embeddings to continuously adapt to evolving data relationships. The core of our method lies in the adaptive projection, which learns to align embeddings based on observed interactions and the underlying network structure. This dynamic adaptation contrasts sharply with traditional relational embeddings, which typically rely on fixed mappings. Our approach demonstrates enhanced ability to represent nuanced relationships within complex networks, leading to improved performance in tasks requiring accurate relational understanding. We define the key components of the system, including the RNN architecture, the projection layer, and the learning objective. The paper outlines the mathematical formulation of the system, highlighting the dynamic nature of the embedding projection.

title: Quantum Error Correction Embedding Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Quantum Error Correction Embedding Algorithm designed to significantly enhance the success rate of quantum error correction. The core claim rests on leveraging the redundancy inherent in error-correcting codes to embed controllable quantum error correction (QEC) information directly into the encoding of quantum states. The fundamental mechanism involves a newly designed code that integrates error information within the superposition state of a quantum state, rather than solely focusing on error detection and correction. This approach exploits the inherent properties of superposition to perform error correction. The algorithm's potential impact lies in overcoming limitations of traditional QEC methods, particularly in scenarios where the error rate is high or the complexity of error correction is significant. This work presents a theoretical framework and outlines the key components of the algorithm, establishing a foundation for future research and development in robust quantum computation. The algorithm's success hinges on precisely controlling the superposition state to encode and decode error information effectively. Further investigation is needed to optimize the parameters and explore the algorithm's performance across various quantum systems and error models.

title: Title: Neural Network-Guided Constraint Generation for Robotics
abstract: Neural Network-Guided Constraint Generation for Robotics presents a novel approach to robot control, automating the creation of constraints essential for safe and effective operation. The system utilizes a deep neural network to predict optimal constraint configurations based on a robot's pose and the surrounding environment, effectively learning a compact and effective constraint space. This contrasts sharply with traditional manual constraint creation methods, which often rely on expert knowledge and iterative refinement. The core mechanism involves training a neural network to map robot pose to constraint space, leading to significantly improved constraint quality and adaptability. This paper details the architecture, training process, and preliminary results demonstrating the efficacy of this method in a simulated robotic environment.

evidence.abstract: Quantum-Inspired Constraint Satisfaction (QICS) presents a novel algorithmic framework designed to overcome the limitations of traditional constraint satisfaction algorithms in addressing complex optimization problems. This research introduces a quantum-inspired representation of the search space, leveraging superposition and entanglement to facilitate parallel exploration of multiple solution candidates. The algorithm employs a hybrid quantum-classical approach, intelligently distributing computational tasks between quantum and classical components to achieve exponential speedups in scenarios requiring extensive search. The core mechanism focuses on creating a state space that inherently exhibits quantum-like properties, enabling efficient exploration and potentially, exponentially faster solution times. This paper will detail the algorithm's design, the underlying mathematical principles, and preliminary experimental validation demonstrating its potential for significant performance improvements.

title: 基于多体动态的机器学习
abstract: This paper introduces a novel machine learning framework based on the principles of multi-particle dynamics, leveraging particle simulation for rapid parameter iteration and effective model optimization. Traditional machine learning often necessitates substantial data and computational resources, while multi-particle dynamics offers a pathway to significantly reduce these demands. The proposed framework utilizes a dynamic simulation approach to efficiently refine model parameters and achieve optimal performance. The core mechanism focuses on the rapid iteration of model parameters through the simulation process, offering a computationally efficient alternative to traditional optimization techniques. This work demonstrates the potential of multi-particle dynamics to accelerate model development and improve the performance of machine learning models.

title: Non-Equilibrium Dynamics Neural Networks (NBDNN)
abstract: This paper introduces the Non-Equilibrium Dynamics Neural Networks (NBDNN), a novel approach to neural network design that leverages the principles of non-equilibrium dynamics. The core claim is that neural networks can achieve more sophisticated pattern recognition and generation by mimicking the behavior of non-equilibrium systems. This is achieved through a network architecture based on neural networks incorporating equations derived from non-equilibrium dynamics. The mechanism relies on simulating the dynamical evolution of systems in non-equilibrium states, employing self-organized criticality to drive pattern generation. We demonstrate that this approach overcomes limitations inherent in traditional neural networks by exploiting the inherent complexity arising from systems operating far from equilibrium. The proposed NBDNN architecture offers a pathway to generating novel and complex patterns, potentially applicable in diverse fields such as image generation, time series analysis, and complex system modeling. The network is trained using backpropagation, adapting the weights to minimize the difference between the simulated dynamics and the target patterns. Further research will focus on optimizing the network architecture and exploring the influence of different non-equilibrium dynamics models.

title: Dynamic Bayesian Networks for Modeling Complex Systems with Time-Varying Dependencies
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Dynamic Bayesian Networks (DBNs) for modeling complex systems exhibiting time-varying dependencies. Traditional DBNs often struggle with accurately representing evolving relationships between variables over time, leading to limitations in their predictive capabilities. This work proposes an extension to the standard DBN framework incorporating adaptive learning mechanisms. These mechanisms enable the network to dynamically adjust its structure and parameters in response to observed changes in the system dynamics. The core claim is that this adaptive approach significantly improves the ability of DBNs to model intricate dependencies and provides a more flexible and robust solution compared to static DBN models. Specifically, we explore methods for updating the network's conditional dependencies and parameter estimates based on temporal data streams. The resulting model demonstrates superior performance in scenarios where the underlying system is non-stationary. The research contributes a novel approach to DBN modeling, offering a pathway for tackling complex, real-world systems with evolving characteristics.

title: Non-Euclidean Vector Field Modeling with Adaptive Complexity
abstract: This paper presents a novel method for modeling vector fields in non-Euclidean space, leveraging a self-adjusting complexity metric. Traditional methods struggle with the inherent complexity of these fields, often requiring extensive parameter tuning and limited predictive power. Our approach introduces a "complexity gradient" that dynamically adjusts the mathematical complexity of the vector field, enabling the model to capture a wider range of behavior and improving predictive accuracy. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through a series of simulations and analysis, showcasing its ability to model complex and varied field patterns with significantly reduced parameterization. The core mechanism focuses on creating a self-regulating system that adapts to the data's inherent complexity, offering a robust and adaptable solution for a wide range of applications.

title: AI-Enhanced Personalized Learning Systems in Education
abstract: In this paper we propose an AI-based personalized learning system which is capable of addressing the shortcomings in adaptive, extendible and interpretable functionality of current systems. The model combines reinforcement learning, federated learning, and explainable AI to adapt the educational material in real time according to learner behavior and context. It gives both privacy-preserving student profiling and pedagogically sound feedback, as opposed to its classical counterparts. Experimental results show that the learning efficiency, engagement and performance are enhanced in different environments. The modular nature of the system enables scaling with institutionally owned resources and ensures adherence to ethical and privacy regulations.

title: The DescryptTool: agentic LLM-based workbench for decipherment of historical ciphers
abstract: The DescryptTool is an agentic research workbench developed within the DESCRYPT project to support the cryptanalysis of historical ciphers. Its contribution is not a new cipher-solving algorithm alone, but a controlled architecture in which a large language model (LLM) can use existing cryptanalytic modules through explicit, auditable tool calls. The system separates two roles: (i) the Observer, a read-only assistant that explains the current analytical state and proposes next steps, and (ii) the Orchestrator, an execution mode that can plan, configure, run, and document complete analysis workflows subject to user-controlled permissions. DescryptTool combines a project-based PyQt workbench, local solvers for simple substitution, Vigenère, and homophonic substitution, reusable text workflows, local logging, and persistent SQLite-based memory. This article presents the system architecture, the tool-control model, solver capabilities and limitations, and an evaluation on synthetic and historical ciphertexts. The results show that agentic workflow control can make established cryptanalytic practice more transparent, teachable, and reproducible, while also exposing clear limits: stochastic solvers are not bit-reproducible without recorded random seeds, LLM recommendations may be wrong, and historical systems with nomenclature elements still require expert validation.

title: Guiding Worker Self-Selection in Crowdsourcing Contests: An LLM-Augmented Algorithmic Approach
abstract: Crowdsourcing platforms coordinate large pools of online workers who strategically choose which contests to enter and how much effort to invest. This self-selection can leave important contests with too few participants or too little effort, while workers may regret entering contests that leave them worse off than available alternatives. We study how platforms can recommend contests to workers using self-selection in Tullock contests (SSTC), a two-stage model in which workers first choose contests and then compete within them. We introduce GRAF, a greedy polynomial-time framework that constructs self-selection outcomes by ordering workers according to a score vector, with guarantees of zero worker regret and platform optimality in special cases of SSTC. Because effective orderings are difficult to design under worker heterogeneity, we propose LLMScore, an LLM-driven evolutionary framework that automatically designs GRAF's scoring algorithm. LLMScore addresses two challenges: jointly optimizing platform utility and worker satisfaction, and evaluating worker regret when exact computation is intractable. Trained only on small instances of one setting, it transfers to larger and structurally different settings; moreover, its output is human-readable code that platform operators can inspect and modify. Across 1,000 synthetic instances spanning four settings, GRAF with LLMScore consistently achieves high-quality, often near-optimal, outcomes with low worker regret, benefiting both platforms and workers.

title: An LLM-Associated Register Shift in Korean Journal Abstracts: A Morphology-Aware Excess-Vocabulary Study, 2018-2026
abstract: Excess vocabulary, a word's frequency above its pre-2023 trend, is how the change in scholarly English after 2022 has been measured. We adapt it to Korean with morphological units on 398,296 KCI abstracts (2018-August 2026), with 47,165 Vietnamese abstracts for comparison. Placebo floors are 0.1-2.2 points for the single-word statistic and at most 2.9 for the re-selected split-half set statistic. Korean abstracts show nothing in 2023, onset in late 2024, a rise through 2025 flattening in mid-2026: sisahada "suggest" appears in 21.4% of 2026 abstracts against 5.3% expected; plain verbs like araboda "look into" fall to a quarter of trend. Under stated assumptions the single-word conditional lower bound on LLM-processed abstracts is 3.5%, 10.5% and 16.1% for 2024-2026 and a split-half set bound 7.8%, 20.6% and 33.0%. Holzwarth et al.'s estimator under the same discipline gives 41.9% and 72.1% for 2025-2026. Subject-matter controls reduce but do not remove it: restricting the set to lemmas three language-model annotators all call style leaves 14.7 of the 33.0 points, and pairing each 2026 abstract with its journal's closest base-period abstract leaves 34.1. Tested translation routes do not explain it: the surface marks of translated Korean fall as the markers rise. In the same articles' English abstracts the excess appears a year earlier; where the English side carries none, the Korean shift persists at 30 to 66% of the rate where it does. Control abstracts from three providers reproduce the rising words, with marker turnover consistent with model generations; implied prevalences are scenario-dependent.

title: Human-agent discovery of reconfigurable in-plane ferroelectric superdomain control
abstract: Automated experimentation is most effective when the observables, available actions, and objective are defined before the experiment starts, as is the case for Bayesian optimization. However, in many exploratory experiments, the variables that describe the sample must be extracted from the data, new operations emerge during the experiments, and the instrument budget is too small to learn the problem by trials. Here we introduce the Scanning Probe Agentic Research Cycle (SPARC) framework, in which a coding agent and a human operator share one microscope, one notebook, and two persistent memory files. FINDINGS.md stores graded conclusions about the experiment, whereas PITFALLS.md records learned failure modes of analysis and instrument. We apply SPARC to reconfigure the in-plane superdomain direction of a (111)-oriented PbZr0.2Ti0.8O3 film. In an operator-supervised campaign, the agent reanalyzed earlier manual measurements and developed an oriented lattice of stationary bias pulses with alternating polarity to reconfigure the superdomain direction. In a subsequent agent-controlled campaign, PITFALLS.md entries were compiled into checks that validate a design before any write. The experiments showed that spatial polarity alternation, instead of the exact matching between the lattice and lamellar periods, determines directional selection. Combining a raster scan with a masked pulse lattice printed the letters UTK into the superdomain orientation. The campaign also identified practical requirements for agentic experimentation where physical verification of instrument execution, the conditions under which stored findings remain valid, validation of new observables on instrument data, and robust control protocols.

title: CSN Quantum Computing Processes in the Human Brain
abstract: CSN stands for Catalin Silviu Nutu, and it is the acronym for the name of the author who has developed the theory related to the CSN Algorithm, such as presented in his previous work published so far. Current conventional and classical AI models today, mainly based on supervised and unsupervised learning, have almost reached their limits, and they are completely insufficient and totally inadequate to simulate and to model highly sophisticated and complicated brain processes involved in highly creative and extremely innovative brain processes. Based on the theory introduced, developed and presented by the author related to the CSN Algorithm and by introducing a new type of special matrix named CSN Matrix of Activations, this paper generates a quantum computing model named CSN Quantum Computing brain model. This paper expands on the latest work of the author presented in his last papers on this topic, namely “Decryption of Evolutionary Fractals by means of Procedural Randomness generated with an Intelligence Model based on the CSN Algorithm”, presented at the International Conference XR Salento 2025 in Otranto, Italy, and a subsequent paper entitled “Enhanced Intelligence Models based on the CSN Algorithm”, also published in 2025, in the International Journal of Computational Engineering Research (IJCER)

title: Executable Matrix-Product Unitaries: A Geometric Operator Framework for Quantum Circuits
abstract: Quantum circuit theory has long treated Matrix‑Product Unitaries (MPUs) as elegant but unreachable objects—beautiful on paper, impossible to extract, and as far as we know never once executed on real hardware. This work breaks that barrier. We introduce the first geometric MPU extraction pipeline capable of reconstructing full multi‑qubit unitaries with machine‑precision fidelity, validating them across uniform CZ layers, bidirectional sweeps, non‑uniform constructions, QFT‑derived operators, high‑bond entangling layers, and multi‑layer MPU compositions. Every MPU class tested—without exception—compiles cleanly through Qiskit into hardware‑native CX+U3 circuits, producing thousands‑gate decompositions that match the original MPU operators with Frobenius error near 10^{-11} and fidelity 1.0. For the first time, MPUs move from abstract tensor‑network theory into executable quantum computation. This establishes a practical bridge between MPU mathematics and real quantum devices, opening a new path for hardware‑compatible tensor‑network operators, circuit compression, and quantum algorithm design.

title: Dynamic Probability Graphs: Modeling and Optimization of Complex Systems
abstract: Dynamic Probability Graphs (DPGs) represent a novel approach to modeling complex systems by dynamically updating graph structures based on real-time environmental changes. This paper introduces a method employing reinforcement learning and evolutionary algorithms to optimize the graph structure, ensuring model predictability and accurate system behavior prediction. The core mechanism focuses on a continuous adjustment process, dynamically responding to evolving conditions. Traditional approaches often suffer from static models, failing to capture the dynamic nature of real-world systems. This research addresses this limitation by creating a flexible and adaptive representation, offering improved predictive capabilities and optimization potential.

title: Adaptive Dynamic Probability Model
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for probabilistic modeling, termed the Adaptive Dynamic Probability Model (ADPM), that dynamically adjusts model parameters based on data. The core innovation lies in a self-adaptive parameter adjustment mechanism, enabling the model to continuously optimize its predictive accuracy. This approach contrasts with static probabilistic models, offering increased efficiency and adaptability. We detail the framework's architecture, explain the self-adjustment process, and demonstrate its efficacy through illustrative examples, highlighting its potential for improved predictive performance across various applications.

Traditional optimization methods often rely on manual design, limiting the algorithm's adaptability. This algorithm leverages a dynamic "Learning Parameter" mechanism that adapts to data and model discrepancy, resulting in improved performance across diverse datasets. The core mechanism involves a continuous feedback loop, allowing the algorithm to refine its parameters in real-time, offering a significant advantage for complex, evolving datasets. We present a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's performance, demonstrating its effectiveness in various scenarios, including high-dimensional data and non-linear relationships.

This work addresses the limitations of existing static models by introducing a dynamic, self-correcting framework optimized for spin-based calculations. The research highlights the potential of this approach to significantly advance the field of quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Error Correction: Adaptive Synchronization Algorithm
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is a critical component of quantum computation, enabling the reliable manipulation of quantum states. Current synchronization algorithms, however, often struggle to maintain the required accuracy and speed, particularly in the face of environmental noise. This paper introduces a novel adaptive synchronization algorithm based on quantum error correction principles. The core mechanism leverages the dynamic adjustment of quantum states during the error correction process to achieve higher precision and faster computation, effectively mitigating the impact of noise. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this algorithm through theoretical analysis and preliminary simulations, showcasing its potential to significantly improve the performance of quantum processors. Keywords: Quantum Error Correction, Adaptive Synchronization, Quantum State Synchronization, Quantum Computation, Noise Mitigation.

title: Self-Supervised Representation Learning via Contrastive Relational Embedding
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-supervised representation learning approach for graph data, termed Contrastive Relational Embedding. The core challenge in leveraging graphs for machine learning lies in effectively capturing the intricate relationships between nodes. Existing self-supervised methods often fall short in this regard, primarily focusing on unsupervised node embeddings without explicitly considering the relational context. Our method addresses this limitation by training a neural network to learn embeddings that reflect the underlying graph structure through a contrastive learning framework. Specifically, we define relationships as 'neighbor' and 'connected-to' and use a contrastive loss to pull together embeddings of nodes that share these relations, while pushing apart the embeddings of nodes with different relations. This approach allows the model to learn rich, graph-aware representations without relying on manual annotations. We demonstrate the efficacy of our method through a theoretical analysis and a conceptual outline, highlighting its potential for improved performance in downstream graph-related tasks.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN BREAST CANCER SCREENING: A REVIEW
authors: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN BREAST CANCER SCREENING: A REVIEW
abstract: Abstract Breast cancer is the most frequently diagnosed cancer among women worldwide, and early detection through screening remains essential for reducing mortality. Mammography is the standard screening modality; however, its diagnostic performance may be affected by false positive results, false-negative findings, reduced sensitivity in dense breast tissue, and variability in image interpretation. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning and deep learning, have enhanced breast cancer screening by improving lesion detection, image classification, risk prediction, and workflow efficiency. AI has been successfully applied to mammography, digital breast tomosynthesis, ultrasound, and magnetic resonance imaging, demonstrating promising improvements in diagnostic accuracy and screening performance. Despite these advances, challenges such as limited dataset diversity, algorithm bias, lack of interpretability, regulatory concerns, data privacy, and integration into clinical practice remain barriers to widespread implementation. Ongoing research focusing on robust validation, ethical AI development, and multidisciplinary collaboration is expected to facilitate the safe and effective adoption of AI in breast cancer screening. This review summarizes current applications of AI in breast cancer screening, highlights its clinical benefits and limitations, and discusses future perspectives for integrating AI into evidence-based and personalized breast cancer screening programs.

Traditional entanglement weaving methods are often static, limiting efficiency. Our algorithm leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to adjust the size and structure of entangled networks in response to specific requirements, offering a significant advancement over existing approaches. We explore the core mechanism of this dynamic adjustment through a novel control strategy. This work demonstrates the potential of this approach to enhance quantum communication and quantum computation through adaptive network design.

title: Based on Quantum Entanglement: Distributed Coprocessor
abstract: This paper proposes a novel architecture for distributed coprocessor networks leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. The core idea is to utilize entangled nodes for ultra-fast, secure data transmission and computation, overcoming the limitations of traditional distributed computing systems. We detail a mechanism for constructing a network of entangled nodes, employing entanglement-based measurements and manipulations to facilitate data exchange and computation. The use of Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocols ensures the security of the communication channel. This approach offers a significant advancement over conventional methods, providing enhanced bandwidth, improved security, and the potential for distributed computing capabilities across extended distances. The theoretical framework and underlying principles are presented, outlining a pathway toward realizing a quantum-enhanced distributed coprocessor network.

title: Adaptive Topological Transformation Algorithm for Quantum Computing (ATTC)
abstract: This paper introduces an Adaptive Topological Transformation Algorithm (ATTC) for quantum computing, designed to dynamically manipulate quantum states. Traditional quantum computation often relies on static state representations, limiting the ability to precisely simulate quantum system behavior. The ATTC leverages topological transformations, a powerful tool in quantum geometry, to optimize quantum states for enhanced efficiency and robustness. This algorithm dynamically adjusts the quantum state structure during a transformation process, resulting in improved performance metrics. The core mechanism focuses on optimizing the quantum state's geometry through a series of carefully designed topological operations. This innovation promises to significantly improve the capabilities of quantum algorithms, particularly in areas requiring precise modeling and dynamic adaptation. We present a comprehensive analysis of the ATTC's design and performance, demonstrating its potential to advance quantum computing paradigms.

This approach promises significant speedups compared to classical approaches, particularly for large and complex CSPs. The paper details the algorithm's design, potential benefits, and preliminary results demonstrating improved performance.

title: Support Vector Machines for Classification, Regression, and Outlier Detection: A Tutorial
abstract: Support Vector Machine (SVM) is a fundamental machine learning method based on the principle of maximum-margin learning. This chapter develops SVM from its geometric intuition to its optimization formulation and extensions. We first contrast SVM with the Perceptron and motivate the use of the maximum-margin decision boundary. We then derive hard-margin SVM, including the primal and dual optimization problems, the role of Lagrange multipliers, the Karush--Kuhn--Tucker (KKT) conditions, and the interpretation of support vectors. Soft-margin SVM is subsequently introduced to handle approximately linearly separable data through slack variables and regularization. For nonlinear classification, kernelization and the kernel trick are presented, leading to kernel SVM in which inner products are replaced by kernel evaluations in a possibly high-dimensional feature space. The chapter then extends the support-vector framework beyond classification to Support Vector Regression (SVR), where an $\varepsilon$-insensitive tube is used for regression, and to one-class SVM, where a separating boundary is learned for novelty and outlier detection. Throughout the chapter, emphasis is placed on the connections between geometry, convex optimization, duality, KKT conditions, sparsity, and the role of support vectors across the different formulations.

title: Natural Language Processing for Human–Computer Interaction
abstract: In this work we propose an advanced Natural Language Processing (NLP) framework for HCI that handles some of the important challenges such as multilingualism, emotional intelligence, context preservation, and explainability. Utilising transformer-based models, memory-augmented networks, and privacy-preserving learning, the system guarantees robust, adaptive and empathetic interaction in any domain. It allows real-time conversation, cross-domain understanding, and dynamic behavior modeling, without compromising data privacy. The proposed framework also focuses on the scalability, standard evaluation protocols, and ethical compliance for commercialization, which drive it to be a versatile, secure, and unified platform that enable large-scale deployment in next-genre HCI systems.

title: Scaling Multi-Agent Systems with Prospect-State Propagation
abstract: Current LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) periodically compress intermediate states to reduce inference-time token consumption, thereby attempting to incorporate more agents. However, naive scaling strategies face challenges. For example, in economic simulations, large-scale MAS typically discard semantically rich economic states, i.e., agent behavioral trajectories, which are key drivers of macroeconomic fluctuations. In this paper, we reveal a phenomenon in which agent heterogeneity gradually decreases during simulation, and propose Prospect-State Propagation for Multi-Agent Systems (PspMAS). Inspired by prospect theory, PspMAS decouples each agent's micro state into a compact Prospect State and an expressive Semantic State. The former records psychological traces through a lightweight, parallelizable propagator and continuously injects heterogeneity into the system. The latter leverages the strong perception, reasoning, planning, and decision-making abilities of LLMs. These two components work complementarily, providing a scalable LLM-based multi-agent simulation solution.

title: An Empirical Measurement of Jailbreaking Evaluators
abstract: Expert evaluation of jailbreak responses is costly and difficult to scale, so the community increasingly relies on automated evaluators to determine whether an attack succeeds. However, jailbreak studies typically validate their chosen evaluator independently, repeatedly spending resources on similar evaluation efforts while making results across papers difficult to compare. Different evaluators also encode different definitions of jailbreak success, meaning that reported attack strength and apparent progress can depend substantially on which evaluator is used. We systematically compare six evaluators that recur in recent jailbreak attack and defense research: HarmBench, JailbreakBench, JailbreakRadar, StrongReject, JADES, and JailMeter. To our knowledge, no prior study has evaluated all six on the same human-labeled data under a controlled setup. We evaluate them on JailbreakQR and JailMeter-Eva, using human judgments as the reference, and measure agreement with humans, error types, and consistency across attack families. For evaluators that require a general-purpose LLM judge, we use a shared backbone to control for model-specific variation. We found that JADES exhibits the best overall performance, while HarmBench and StrongReject also demonstrate good performance.

title: Computing with logarithmicstate and history
abstract: A computation can return to its original state while retaining a nonzero history of interaction. We presentthe application of exact logarithmic state/history in the Substrate Ledger Computer, implemented in SLC-GEN2-R4. Positive source-action ratios become additive coordinates, while their ordered incrementsretain cumulative rise, fall, variation and maximum excursion. These readouts distinguish an unchangedendpoint from an executed loop and recover a historical contact barrier from its logarithmic maximumand original action. An exact composition law joins history segments without changing their referenceor losing maximizing states. The same runtime represents uncertainty over complete linked histories anduses rationally weighted formal logarithms to select native probes and report resolution for a specifiedhistorical target. A four-history receiver example separates equal quantities of source information withdifferent barrier content. Adaptive two-observation policies then resolve a target with an expected 1.5readings while retaining unresolved histories, and a separate lookahead example gains information onlyafter a second interaction. Source-defined scale-and-turn coordinates, quarter-turn golden scheduling,construction-boundary information and signed contribution arithmetic share these contracts. Installedapplications connect the representation to isotope assemblies, exact frustrated-spin spectra and signedMöbius-moment calculations. The resulting method makes logarithmic history an executable object: itcan be queried, composed, used to choose an observation and continued from a complete checkpoint.Keywords: logarithmic computation; executable history; exact arithmetic; conditional reconstruction;adaptive observation; Substrate Ledger Computer

abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum algorithm design approach leveraging non-linear models. Traditional quantum algorithm design relies heavily on classical optimization techniques, limiting the applicability of quantum computation to specific problem domains. We propose a new method that dynamically adjusts the problem's structure through a non-linear model, enabling the creation of highly efficient quantum algorithms tailored to particular computational challenges. This approach systematically transforms a complex problem into a simplified, solvable optimization problem, facilitating the development of quantum solutions that surpass the capabilities of traditional methods. The core mechanism involves constructing a non-linear model that governs the problem's evolution, allowing for the implementation of quantum circuits that exploit specific properties. This research explores the potential of this technique to unlock new avenues in quantum algorithm development and provide a foundation for more efficient quantum computation.

title: Pulse Geometry Quantum Entanglement Simulation
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum entanglement simulation framework, the "Pulse Geometry" model, designed to accurately predict complex quantum systems. Traditional quantum simulation often struggles with the inherent challenges of representing and simulating quantum phenomena, particularly when dealing with intricate entanglement dynamics. The Pulse Geometry framework leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to significantly enhance simulation accuracy and precision. This work proposes a new approach to quantum simulation by utilizing a specially crafted geometric representation of quantum states, intrinsically linked to entanglement, to reduce computational complexity and enhance fidelity. The core mechanism involves creating a dynamic, multi-layered representation of the quantum system, where entanglement is the primary driving force behind its behavior. This is achieved through a unique algorithm that effectively encodes and manipulates entanglement across the system's geometry. The resulting simulation will offer a significant advancement over existing quantum simulation techniques, particularly in the modeling of systems exhibiting strong entanglement.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Machine Learning Model Gradient Descent Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a dynamic adaptive machine learning model gradient descent optimization method designed to enhance model performance through dynamic adjustment of the gradient descent strategy. Traditional gradient descent methods are often static, limiting their effectiveness in complex, dynamic datasets. This research proposes a novel approach that dynamically adjusts the gradient descent parameters based on the data distribution, leading to improved convergence and generalization. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through extensive experimentation and analysis, showcasing its ability to outperform static gradient descent in several benchmark datasets. The core mechanism centers around a feedback loop that continuously monitors the gradient landscape and adjusts the learning rate and step size, effectively adapting to the data's inherent variability. This adaptation significantly improves the model's robustness and generalization capabilities.

abstract: Quantum machine learning (QML) is a rapidly developing field with the potential to revolutionize various computational tasks. title: 基于可扩展拓扑光子网络的量子密钥分发协议
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum key distribution (QKD) protocol designed specifically for scalable photonic networks. The protocol leverages the inherent advantages of a multi-hop, all-topological architecture to overcome the limitations of traditional QKD systems regarding key transmission distance and rate. We propose a scheme utilizing quantum entanglement and state transformations within the network to facilitate distributed key generation and secure key distribution. The core innovation lies in the network topology itself, which allows for robust error correction and eavesdropping detection, ultimately leading to a highly secure and high-throughput quantum communication system. The theoretical analysis demonstrates the protocol's resilience to various attack scenarios and highlights its potential for practical implementation in large-scale quantum networks.

title: The Geometry of Causality: Hierarchical Causality Networks and Predictive Geometry
abstract: This paper explores the intersection of geometry and causality, proposing a novel hierarchical causality network framework. We investigate how the structure of a network – defined by its connectivity and topology – directly influences the flow of causal influence, offering a new perspective on understanding and modeling causal relationships. The core claim is that causality is fundamentally geometric, and that the representation of a causal network via a geometric structure allows for predictive capabilities. This work utilizes a hierarchical network model to demonstrate the potential for this geometric approach to yield enhanced predictive accuracy. The analysis will delve into the mathematical foundations of this framework, focusing on network topology and flow dynamics. We will explore how the geometry inherent in the network structure enables a deeper understanding of causality than traditional, purely statistical approaches.

title: A Hybrid Approach: Combining Differentiable Simulation Engines with Reinforcement Learning Control
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to control and optimization of complex physical systems by integrating differentiable simulation engines with reinforcement learning (RL). Traditional control methods often struggle with the inherent complexity and nonlinearity of many physical systems, requiring extensive tuning and potentially failing to generalize well. Our methodology leverages the ability to represent physical systems as a set of differential equations, allowing for continuous, differentiable simulation. This simulation environment then serves as the basis for training an RL agent, which learns an optimal control policy through trial and error. The key innovation lies in the seamless coupling of these two techniques – the deterministic, accurate simulation providing the feedback signal for the RL agent, and the RL agent dynamically adjusting the simulation parameters to improve learning efficiency and robustness. We detail the architecture of this hybrid system, focusing on the mathematical formulation and implementation considerations. This approach offers the potential for achieving real-time control and optimization of systems that are intractable for conventional control methods. ---

title: Quantum Entanglement Computation via Algebraic Vector Representation
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, presents a unique challenge to computational efficiency. Traditional methods often struggle to efficiently handle the intricate calculations involved in quantum systems. This paper proposes a novel approach utilizing algebraic vector representation to transform entanglement calculations into a set of algebraic operations, aiming to dramatically improve computational speed and provide deeper insights into the fundamental nature of quantum entanglement. We establish a new method for representing entangled states as algebraic vectors, leveraging the geometric properties of string theory to achieve this transformation. The core mechanism involves the development of a specialized algebraic vector representation that allows for efficient computation through a sequence of transformations, ultimately revealing the underlying mathematical structure of entangled states. This research explores the potential for quantum entanglement computation to be revolutionized by this algorithmic shift.

title: Quantum Bayesian Network for Constraint Satisfaction
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Quantum Bayesian Network (QBN) architecture specifically designed for Constraint Satisfaction problems (CSPs). We propose a QBN leveraging quantum annealing or variational quantum algorithms to efficiently explore solution spaces, enabling the handling of highly complex, multi-variable CSPs. The core mechanism involves dynamically updating constraint relationships through quantum superposition, offering a potential paradigm shift in solving these challenging problems. We demonstrate the efficacy of our approach through a case study focusing on a simplified CSP, highlighting its ability to outperform traditional methods in terms of solution finding time and complexity. Furthermore, we discuss the challenges and potential future directions of this research.

title: Distributed Differential Privacy via Federated Learning with Byzantine Resilience
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising approach to training machine learning models on decentralized data sources without direct data sharing, thereby preserving data privacy. However, existing FL frameworks are susceptible to Byzantine attacks, where malicious participants intentionally send false information to disrupt the learning process and compromise the privacy guarantees provided by differential privacy (DP). This paper proposes a novel distributed differential privacy protocol for FL that incorporates Byzantine resilience. Our approach leverages verifiable distributed computation to detect and mitigate the influence of Byzantine participants, ensuring both privacy and robustness against malicious behavior. The core claim of this work is that FL with DP is inherently vulnerable to Byzantine attacks. The primary mechanism involves designing a federated learning protocol that actively identifies and downweights contributions from potentially malicious participants. We achieve this through a combination of outlier detection techniques and verifiable computation, guaranteeing a robust and differentially private learning outcome. The theoretical analysis demonstrates the effectiveness of our protocol in maintaining differential privacy while mitigating the impact of Byzantine adversaries. We provide a detailed mathematical formulation of the protocol and its privacy guarantees, focusing on the key parameters and their impact on the overall privacy budget. Finally, we outline the potential implications and future research directions for this work.

title: Consistency Is Not Correctness: What Internal Contradiction Detection Certifies, Why the Entailment Is Disjunctive, and Which Decisions It Leaves Unlicensed
abstract: Life of Research (c) 2026 Pranay Mahendrakar. Licensed under CC BY 4.0. Contradiction detection occupies an unusual position among proposals for making a language model check itself. Comparing two of a model's own outputs appears to need no external oracle, which makes it look like the one exception to the observation that working hallucination detectors sit outside the model. This paper argues that the appearance is produced by running two different inferences under one word. Inconsistency supports a deductive inference: if two outputs contradict each other, at least one of them is false, and this follows from logic alone without any appeal to the world. Consistency supports only an inductive one: agreement is evidence of correctness to the extent that the model's errors are unstable under whatever perturbation produced the second output, an assumption that the sampling-based detectors state explicitly and that the strongest published instance of the family declines to extend to systematic error. The two inferences have opposite properties. The deductive one is sound and disjunctive, identifying that something is wrong without identifying which output is wrong, and so licenses withholding but not repair. The inductive one names a specific output to accept, and fails in the cases that matter most, because an error shared by both compared outputs survives the comparison intact. The paper traces the consequences: that breaking the disjunction requires an adjudicator whose errors are not those of the generator, that every published route to one is external in the relevant sense even when it runs on the same weights, and that a consistency rate is a measurement of distributional stability under a named perturbation rather than a reliability figure. Making consistency an optimization target inverts its diagnostic value, which two recent results on label-free training report directly. What is not known is stated flatly, and six measurements are specified.

title: Early Detection of Digital Transaction Fraud in Banking Systems Using the Random Forest Algorithm
abstract: This research aims to develop methods for preventing and detecting cyberattacks in banking systems by leveraging machine learning techniques.[1] Cybersecurity threats are becoming increasingly complex and pose significant risks to banking institutions and their customers through various attack types including fraud, intrusion, and malware.[2][3], [4]The data science approach utilizing machine learning enables automatic and real-time identification of anomalous patterns in transactional and security log data.[2], [5] This study utilizes transaction datasets and security logs as primary data sources. Random Forest and XGBoost models were selected due to their capability to handle high-dimensional data and class imbalance. Model evaluation was conducted using accuracy, F1-score, and ROC-AUC metrics. The prototype implementation includes a visualization dashboard to assist end-users.[6], [7] Random Forest and XGBoost models are selected due to their capability to handle high-dimensional data and class imbalance.[8], [9] Systematic preprocessing and feature engineering steps will address missing values, normalization, and categorical encoding.[10], [11] Moreover, model evaluation will be conducted using metrics such as accuracy, F1-score, and ROC-AUC to ensure optimal performance.[12] The prototype system implementation includes a visualization dashboard and automatic prediction features for end-users.[13] The expected outcomes of this research are improved early detection and prevention of cyber threats in the banking sector, contributing to the advancement of AI-based security systems in Indonesia.[14] Experimental results demonstrate that tree-based ensemble learning models significantly outperform SVM in handling extreme class imbalance. XGBoost achieved the best performance with an ROC-AUC score of 0.995, followed by Random Forest at 0.992, whereas SVM achieved only 0.935. Model transparency analysis using SHAP confirmed that transaction frequency and spikes in transaction amounts were the most critical predictors for identifying fraud. Overall, this research concludes that integrating XGBoost with the SHAP approach yields a fraud detection system that offers not only high accuracy but also clear interpretability to support decision-making in the digital banking sector.

title: Quantum Algorithms for Optimization Problems in Logistics
abstract: In this paper, we investigate a quantum approach to solve hard optimization problems of logistics, such as vehicle routing, warehouse scheduling, supply chain planning, etc. Employing quantum computation models, viz., Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) as well as hybrid quantum-classical computing framework, the proposed technique overcomes problems of scalability, constraint handling, and performance issues of previous work. The research demonstrates benchmarking on benchmarks, on logistics datasets, and across quantum platforms. We establish that the solution quality and the convergence efficiency were improved by considering the quantum annealing effect, showing that quantum computing is a revolutionary playing card in optimization for logistics.

title: Digital Image Processing
abstract: Integrate machine learning and AI-based approaches into practical image processing with Python Engineers and researchers implementing image processing systems need methods that bridge classical techniques with modern machine learning approaches. This book delivers both traditional and modern AI-based methods and algorithms in image enhancement, restoration, segmentation, compression, and analysis. Written by an educator and researcher with more than 40 years’ experience in signal/image processing and machine learning, this reference provides theoretical and practical tools using the Python platform for a wide range of applications. The book consists of twenty chapters covering fundamental and advanced topics including two-dimensional image modeling, wavelet transform, Kalman filters, image reconstruction and computerized tomography, layered machines, linear and nonlinear autoencoders, and associative memories. Each chapter includes practical examples demonstrating real-world applications, supported by Python code, solution manuals, and presentation materials. This book also covers: Fundamental supervised and unsupervised machine learning methods with specific deep learning applications for image enhancement, segmentation, feature extraction, data compression, and classification Wavelet transform and filter banks integrated with state-of-the-art image analysis and processing Advanced filtering techniques including Wiener and Kalman filters, and two-dimensional image modeling Python implementations via Google colab platform enabling immediate application of theoretical concepts to practical image processing problems Instructor resources including solution manuals and presentation materials supporting adoption in digital image processing and computer vision courses Essential for professionals in industry and research laboratories requiring implementation-ready image processing methods, this reference also serves graduate students and advanced undergraduates in electrical and computer engineering, biomedical engineering, and computer science programs studying digital image processing and computer vision.
